findings.title: The hearts become one hardened state
findings.claim: The ayah presents the possessed hearts as a single hardened receiving state.
findings.mechanism: The carrier qāsiyatan is a feminine singular active participle functioning as the second object-state after jaʿalnā; its singular predicate gathers the plural hearts into one condition, so the response reaches their receptivity as a whole.
findings.reader_payoff: Hardness becomes a condition of reception, not merely a description of mood.
findings.containment: This specifies the local predicate-state; it does not make every hard-heart formulation identical.

epistemic.reason: The focus word-analysis record and its QAC alignment directly support the participial state and its relation to the possessed hearts.

findings.title: Distortion remains ongoing
findings.claim: The ayah portrays the displacement of the words as continuing conduct.
findings.mechanism: The carrier yuḥarrifūna is an imperfect Form II plural verb; its caused-action form contacts the word object and the following ʿan phrase, making the act an ongoing shifting away rather than a completed isolated event.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees distortion as a practice that continues after the earlier breach.
findings.containment: The claim concerns the focus verb's aspect and causative form; it does not generalize the supplied comparison texts.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis identifies the imperfect Form II form and its local object and separation relation.

findings.title: The definite object is a field of word-units
findings.claim: The distortion falls on a definite collective field of word-units.
findings.mechanism: The carrier al-kalima is the definite accusative object of yuḥarrifūna; the article and collective noun contact the distortion verb to specify what is being shifted as word-material, rather than leaving the object as an unspecified idea.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can locate the alteration in the ayah's words themselves.
findings.containment: This keeps the local collective-object reading; it does not expand the noun into all discourse or make the bodily wound association literal.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the definite accusative parse, collective force, and focus-level containment.

findings.title: Words are shifted away
findings.claim: The distortion is framed as separation away from an assigned position.
findings.mechanism: The carrier ʿan is a separation preposition governing the place phrase; in contact with yuḥarrifūna it turns alteration into movement away from a location, so the words are understood as displaced from where they belong.
findings.reader_payoff: A flat statement about changing words gains a spatial direction: away from a place.
findings.containment: The spatial relation is local to the supplied prepositional construction; it does not assert a physical relocation of written objects.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly identifies ʿan's separation function and its focus relation to the positions phrase.

findings.title: The words have assigned coordinates
findings.claim: The ayah treats the words as occupying plural assigned positions.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mawāḍiʿihi is a genitive plural place noun after ʿan, and its attached pronoun ties those positions to the word-material; the place noun contacts the separation preposition to turn meaning into a map of slots from which the words are moved.
findings.reader_payoff: Distortion becomes a violation of arrangement as well as a change of wording.
findings.containment: This uses the local plural place noun and possessive link; it does not claim that every occurrence of the root denotes semantic coordinates.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the plural place-noun parse, pronoun attachment, and local mapping payoff.

findings.title: Distortion and forgetting form a paired diagnosis
findings.claim: The ayah joins word-displacement and forgetting as two coordinated symptoms.
findings.mechanism: The first carrier wa follows the ongoing distortion clause and coordinates it with the perfect forgetting clause; that contact keeps the outward alteration and the lost reminder-share in one diagnostic movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the offenses as related conditions rather than isolated entries in a list.
findings.containment: The conjunction establishes coordination, not a claim that either clause is reducible to the other.

epistemic.reason: The trusted word-analysis record directly assigns the conjunction its local clause-linking function.

findings.title: Forgetting is a completed act of neglect
findings.claim: The ayah records the loss of the reminder-material as an accomplished act of neglect.
findings.mechanism: The carrier nasū is a perfect plural verb; its completed form contacts the passive reminder clause that follows, turning the sequence from received instruction to an act already left aside.
findings.reader_payoff: Forgetting acquires an event-shape and accountability within the clause chain.
findings.containment: This states the focus verb's aspect and local relation; it does not erase the ordinary translation sense of forgetting.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the perfect plural form and its opposition to the reminder field in the focus.

findings.title: The forgotten material is an unmeasured share
findings.claim: What is forgotten is presented as an allotted share whose measure is left open.
findings.mechanism: The carrier ḥaẓẓan is an indefinite accusative object of nasū; its allotment sense contacts the forgetting verb to make the lost material a portion within a larger received whole, named but not quantified.
findings.reader_payoff: The omission feels like a loss of a due portion, not merely a vague lapse.
findings.containment: The focus leaves the size unspecified; the claim does not identify the share beyond the supplied reminder relation.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly supports the indefinite object parse and the allocated-share field.

findings.title: Only a portion comes from the reminder
findings.claim: The forgotten share is a portion drawn from what they were reminded of.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mimmā fuses a partitive preposition with a relative element; its contact with ḥaẓẓan and dhukkirū makes the source of the loss partial while keeping it inside the supplied reminder-content.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold partial omission without reducing it to trivial omission.
findings.containment: The partitive relation does not specify which content was lost or claim that the remainder was preserved intact.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the partitive construction and its local backward relation.

findings.title: Reminder was received before it was lost
findings.claim: The clause foregrounds received reminding before it names the later forgetting.
findings.mechanism: The carrier dhukkirū is passive Form II, suppressing the reminder-agent and presenting the group as recipients; its contact with the active nasū creates a reception-to-neglect sequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The forgotten material appears as something that had reached them, not as an unoffered possibility.
findings.containment: The passive form leaves the agent unspoken; this finding does not identify that agent.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the passive Form II morphology and its relation to the active forgetting verb.

findings.title: The ayah opens inside a consequence
findings.claim: The opening presents the following breach and its aftermath as a resultative continuation.
findings.mechanism: The carrier fa is a result particle at the start of the focus; its contact with the governed breach phrase and the sequence of following verbs makes the ayah read as an unfolding consequence rather than a detached new report.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader enters after a cause has already been established and can feel the aftermath being unpacked.
findings.containment: The result relation is established within the focus opening; this finding does not reconstruct any omitted prior wording.

epistemic.reason: The trusted word-analysis record directly identifies the result particle and its focus-level consequence frame.

findings.title: The pronoun keeps the reminder-content present
findings.claim: The compact pronoun ties the forgotten share back to the content that had been delivered as reminder.
findings.mechanism: The carrier bihi is a prepositional pronoun completing the passive reminder construction; its backward contact with mimmā and dhukkirū keeps the referenced reminder-content active while the clause moves on.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees what the forgotten share belongs to even though the content is not repeated.
findings.containment: The pronoun supplies backward reference, not a new description of the reminder-content.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly supports the pronoun's complement function and compact backward reference.

findings.title: The chain turns toward present address
findings.claim: A conjunction pivots the ayah from completed diagnosis into the addressee's continuing encounter.
findings.mechanism: The second carrier wa follows the completed forgetting clause and precedes the non-cessation frame; its contact with the tense and person shift turns retrospective diagnosis toward present address.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader moves from what they did to what the addressee keeps encountering.
findings.containment: The pivot is local to the conjunction and following frame; it does not assert a wider narrative progression.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the conjunction's position and its local pivot effect.

findings.title: Negation turns cessation into persistence
findings.claim: The negative particle helps form a frame of non-cessation for the discovery that follows.
findings.mechanism: The carrier lā immediately contacts tazālu, whose ordinary cessation field is thereby held under negation; the pair changes the temporal reading from stopping to continued recurrence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears persistence before the discovered treachery is named.
findings.containment: This finding concerns the local lā-plus-tazālu construction and does not duplicate the verb's separate person and aspect contribution.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly identifies the continuative construction and its non-cessation payoff.

findings.title: Discovery remains in the addressee's view
findings.claim: The continuative verb makes the addressee's discovery of treachery an ongoing encounter.
findings.mechanism: The carrier tazālu is an imperfect second-person singular continuative verb; its contact with lā supplies persistence and its person marking opens direct address before the discovery verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah brings the reader from past diagnosis into a continuing act of seeing.
findings.containment: The continuity is local to the supplied construction; it does not claim that every later discovery has the same duration.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the verb's person, aspect, and continuative relation.

findings.title: Discovery rises into view
findings.claim: The discovery verb gives the hidden treachery an upward-coming-into-view quality.
findings.mechanism: The carrier taṭṭaliʿu is a second-person imperfect Form VIII verb; its rising and appearing field contacts the following object relation and makes discovery feel like access to what had been above or concealed.
findings.reader_payoff: Seeing becomes an arrival of hidden conduct into the addressee's field of view.
findings.containment: The elevation is an image carried by the supplied form; it does not turn the object into a literal height claim.

epistemic.reason: The trusted focus analysis supports the Form VIII parse and its local discovery imagery.

findings.title: The discovered act is held before the observer
findings.claim: The object of discovery is framed as something encountered upon the observer's field.
findings.mechanism: The carrier ʿalā governs the indefinite treachery-instance; its superposition relation contacts the elevated-discovery verb and keeps the discovered act before the addressee as the verb's object.
findings.reader_payoff: The discovery gains a positional frame without losing its ordinary meaning of observing treachery.
findings.containment: This is the preposition's local relation, not a claim that the treachery occupies a literal physical surface.

epistemic.reason: The trusted word-analysis record directly supplies the prepositional object relation and its bounded image.

findings.title: Treachery appears one instance at a time
findings.claim: The ayah names an indefinite individual instance of treachery under discovery.
findings.mechanism: The carrier khāʾinatin is an indefinite singular genitive after ʿalā; its singular indefiniteness contacts the discovery frame to present a particular act or occurrence rather than an abstract accusation alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive betrayal as something encountered in concrete instances.
findings.containment: The form leaves the instance unidentified; it does not generalize the accusation to every member.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the indefinite singular parse and its instance-level local effect.

findings.title: The first source phrase places treachery within the group
findings.claim: The first minhum phrase locates the discovered treachery within the named group.
findings.mechanism: The carrier minhum follows the treachery-instance and marks partitive source; its contact with khāʾinatin makes the breach arise from inside the group rather than from an unspecified outside actor.
findings.reader_payoff: The accusation gains an internal location while remaining instance-specific.
findings.containment: The phrase identifies source within the group; it does not make every group member treacherous.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly supports the partitive source relation at this occurrence.

findings.title: The indictment contains its own exception
findings.claim: The accusation is severe while remaining grammatically open to an exception.
findings.mechanism: The carrier illā opens a connected exception after the internal source phrase and before the small class; its contact with the preceding collective description prevents the indictment from swallowing the whole group.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader receives judgment with discrimination already built into its grammar.
findings.containment: The exception is preserved without determining more about the excepted people than the focus states.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the exception particle's position and limiting function.

findings.title: The exception is a small, unmeasured class
findings.claim: The excepted class is marked as few without a stated numerical measure.
findings.mechanism: The carrier qalīlan is an indefinite accusative adjective governed by the exception frame; its smallness contacts illā to make the protected minority real but unquantified.
findings.reader_payoff: The exception has ethical force without becoming a census.
findings.containment: The focus says little, not how many; it does not rank or identify the minority.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the indefinite adjective parse and its qualitative smallness.

findings.title: The breach is the governed ground of response
findings.claim: The opening routes the divine response through the breach as its governed reason.
findings.mechanism: The carrier bi is a causal preposition governing the following breach phrase; its contact with naqḍihim makes the response arise through an assigned cause relation rather than leaving the opening as an unstructured instrument phrase.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the response as connected to a stated ground before the consequences unfold.
findings.containment: This records the causal use in the focus construction; it does not resolve every possible use of the preposition.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly identifies bi's causal government and local relation to the breach phrase.

findings.title: The second source phrase keeps the few inside the group
findings.claim: The repeated minhum phrase locates the exempted few within the same group.
findings.mechanism: The carrier minhum is repeated after qalīlan as a partitive source phrase; its contact with the earlier minhum balances internal treachery with an internal exception, preserving both specificity and shared group location.
findings.reader_payoff: The grammar prevents blanket blame and blanket innocence at once.
findings.containment: The repetition establishes location and contrast; it does not infer the identity or conduct of the few.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the repeated partitive phrase and its balancing function.

findings.title: Diagnosis turns into command
findings.claim: The result particle turns the diagnosis and exception into an immediate mercy command.
findings.mechanism: The carrier fa stands before the imperative iʿfu; its contact with the continuing discovery and the protected exception makes the command a consequence of accurate diagnosis rather than an unrelated appendix.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy enters as the next logical act after seeing clearly.
findings.containment: The result relation does not erase the preceding indictment or decide its legal scope.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly assigns fa its pivot from diagnosis to command.

findings.title: Pardon is commanded as erasure
findings.claim: The first imperative makes pardon an active erasure of the named offense.
findings.mechanism: The carrier iʿfu is a direct second-person imperative; its contact with the immediately prior treachery and the following ʿanhum complement makes the pardon operative as removal of the offense from the account.
findings.reader_payoff: Forgiveness appears as an action to perform, not only an attitude to hold.
findings.containment: The erasure image is bounded to the offense relation in the focus; it does not deny that the treachery was seen.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the direct imperative, its local erasure field, and its focus addressee.

findings.title: Pardon moves the offense away
findings.claim: The pardon idiom marks removal away from the offenders while leaving the offense understood.
findings.mechanism: The carrier ʿanhum completes the prepositional complement after iʿfu; its contact with the preceding treachery lets the offense remain elided while the persons are explicit, so pardon is rendered as taking the offense away from them.
findings.reader_payoff: The command has a direction: the burden is moved away from the people addressed.
findings.containment: The elided offense is recovered only from the local chain; no additional object is supplied.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly supplies the complement relation and its local pardon idiom.

findings.title: Pardon and turning-away are paired
findings.claim: The conjunction pairs pardon with a second mercy operation.
findings.mechanism: The carrier wa joins iʿfu to iṣfaḥ without restating the object; its contact with the two imperatives makes the response cumulative, adding a new act after the first has been commanded.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy becomes a sequence of actions rather than a single undifferentiated response.
findings.containment: The conjunction joins the commands but does not collapse their distinct lexical operations.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly identifies the coordination and its local paired-command payoff.

findings.title: The second mercy command turns the page
findings.claim: The second imperative carries pardon forward as turning away or turning the page.
findings.mechanism: The carrier iṣfaḥ is a direct imperative; its surface-and-page field contacts the preceding iʿfu so the response moves from erasing the offense to turning the encounter forward.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish pardon from the subsequent act of not continuing to face the offense.
findings.containment: The page image remains a bounded lexical resonance; it does not replace the ordinary command to overlook.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the imperative form, paired position, and page/turning field.

findings.title: The ending seals the command with emphasis
findings.claim: The final clause is introduced as an emphatic reason for the mercy command.
findings.mechanism: The carrier inna opens the closing clause after the two imperatives; its contact with the divine subject and love predicate gives the preceding specific command an explicit motivating seal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears mercy followed by the reason its beautiful form is valued.
findings.containment: The particle emphasizes the following clause; it does not by itself specify every relation between the preceding commands and the closure.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis directly supports inna's clause-introducing emphatic function.

findings.title: The divine subject supplies the valuing voice
findings.claim: The closing valuation is explicitly attributed to Allah as the subject of love.
findings.mechanism: The carrier Allāha is governed by inna and functions as the subject of yuḥibbu; its contact with the emphatic closure anchors the valuation in the named divine agent while leaving the local proper-name reading intact.
findings.reader_payoff: The command is framed by whose love gives excellence its final value.
findings.containment: The finding preserves the proper name and its clause role; it does not resolve derivational proposals about the name.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the governed proper-name parse and its subject relation.

findings.title: Love remains a continuing valuation
findings.claim: The closing love predicate presents divine valuation as continuing.
findings.mechanism: The carrier yuḥibbu is an imperfect Form IV predicate; its contact with the definite plural object makes love an ongoing valuation of a class characterized by its conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The closure reads as a continuing standard, not a one-time reaction.
findings.containment: The aspectual claim is local to the predicate; it does not turn the closure into a chronology beyond the focus.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the imperfect predicate and its definite plural object relation.

findings.title: The loved class is defined by beautiful action
findings.claim: The closing object names a definite class of people characterized by producing excellence.
findings.mechanism: The carrier al-muḥsinīna is a definite plural active participle functioning as the object of yuḥibbu; its contact with the love predicate makes beautiful or beneficent action the visible property of the loved class.
findings.reader_payoff: The final category links mercy's form to the kind of conduct the closure values.
findings.containment: The participle names the class in this clause; it does not add an unstated biography or rank within the class.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the definite plural participial form and its object role.

findings.title: The causal opening carries a live syntactic choice
findings.claim: The opening can be heard as a thickened causal surface while the precise function of mā remains open.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mā sits inside bi-mā naqḍihim and can function as a relative element or as an emphatic insertion; in contact with the causal preposition and verbal noun it intensifies the governed reason without changing the breach named.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives added causal weight without being forced to choose between the supplied syntactic analyses.
findings.containment: Both the relative and emphatic possibilities remain live; this finding does not adjudicate the construction.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis explicitly preserves two compatible syntactic functions and states that the local event remains unchanged.

findings.title: The breach is theirs as an act of undoing
findings.claim: The opening assigns covenant breach to them as an active act of undoing.
findings.mechanism: The carrier naqḍihim is a genitive verbal noun after bi, and the attached plural suffix makes the process theirs; its contact with mīthāqahum sets undoing directly against the covenant named next.
findings.reader_payoff: Breach becomes an act that unfastens a formed obligation, not only a label for disobedience.
findings.containment: The unraveling image remains attached to the supplied covenant construction; it does not literalize the covenant as thread.

epistemic.reason: The trusted analysis supplies the gerund, possessive suffix, and local undoing-to-covenant relation.

findings.title: The broken object is a bound covenant
findings.claim: The object of breach is a covenant presented as a trust-binding bond belonging to them.
findings.mechanism: The carrier mīthāqahum is a possessed accusative noun; its suffix ties the covenant to the group, and its binding field contacts naqḍihim so the preceding undoing has a definite load-bearing object.
